dedupe_keys.name: xdi global data centre physical climate risk and adaptation analysis 2025

description: This risk assessment and adaptation-planning case applies a physical climate-risk model to the world's data centres. XDI, a climate-risk analytics company, analysed nearly 9,000 operational and planned data centres and ranked the main data-centre hubs by exposure to hazards such as riverine and surface flooding, coastal inundation, tropical cyclones, forest fires and soil movement, now and in future climate scenarios; it found that hubs such as New Jersey, Hamburg, Shanghai, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Moscow, Bangkok and the Capital Region of Denmark are in the top twenty for risk by 2050, with 20 to 64 per cent of their data centres at high risk of damage, and that more than one in ten data centres in Asia-Pacific is already at high risk. The report, published on 9 July 2025, also quantified how structural adaptations to design and construction reduce projected damage and insurance costs, and a 2026 follow-up examined about 2,600 planned data centres. Coverage: global, present day to 2050 and beyond under emissions scenarios. Format and access: key findings free on the XDI website; the full report is a free download after registration. Caveats: facility locations and design assumptions come from XDI's proprietary database and models, so results cannot be reproduced openly. Simulation uses: hazard exposure screening of data centres, climate adaptation planning of design standards, and resilience inputs for siting studies. Related records: the techUK adaptation report covers UK operators, and the London heatwave and Hurricane Sandy cases show heat and flood impacts.
